purpose: Fifteen accounting handlers declared their body as an inline TypeScript type. An inline type erases to Object at runtime and ValidationPipe skips a parameter whose metatype it cannot transform, so the global pipe validated nothing on any of them. The controller checked what it checked by hand - integer(), instant(), text(), required() - which makes this a narrowing rather than a rescue; the point is the nine call sites that parsed a date as `new Date(body.field)` with no instant(). An unparseable date there is not an error, it is Invalid Date, whose getTime() is NaN, and every comparison against NaN is false - so a guard written as a comparison never fires. V2.2.1 stays FAIL: 51 unvalidated parameters remain across 22 other files.
requiredInvariants: Every constraint is read off what the code already requires, never invented. The money pattern is integer()'s own /^-?\d+$/; the currency pattern is the database's settlement_payment_currency_check /^[A-Z]{3}$/; every enumeration is the policy constant itself via Object.values, not a copy of its values that would drift when the policy gains a member.

No behaviour that worked stops working. Each refusal case is paired with the same body made valid, and the accounting suite passes unchanged at 217. Optional fields stay optional: currency absent still means the controller applies its own RUB default.

The refusal moves to the door, it is not added twice over. Where the controller already refused - service decision, reconciliation answer, attestation gate - the DTO expresses the same rule and the controller keeps its own check, because a DTO guards the pipe and the helper guards the conversion.

A DTO that narrows an enumeration narrows it for a stated reason. RENDERED is absent from the service decision and PREPARED from the reconciliation answer because putting a line back to rendered is undoing an approval, not making a decision - which is what the controller and the policy already refused.
No accounting arithmetic, no policy, no repository and no migration is touched. This is the request boundary only: the controller's parameter types, the DTO classes and their suite.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation, no new dependency; class-validator and the global pipe are both already in use.
acceptance: The defect is proven at the policy, not asserted: evaluatePeriodOpen returns permitted=true with no refusals for a window of two Invalid Dates, and raises neither WINDOW_IS_EMPTY nor WINDOW_OVERLAPS against an existing period, because every one of its comparisons is against NaN. An accounting period with no window passed every refusal the policy had.

All twelve date constraints are bound individually. Each case sends one bad field in an otherwise valid body and asserts the same body with a parseable date resolves - a body with two bad fields would stay green with only one field constrained, which is exactly what the first mutation run showed when removing @IsISO8601 from periodStart left 28 of 28 passing.

Fifteen mutations of the DTO file are caught: nine date constraints plus the three second occurrences (reconciliation window, service reversal), the ServiceKind enumeration, and the money pattern (5 cases). The suite is restored byte-identically after each.
The ratchet moves and is tightened: 66 unvalidated @Body() parameters across 23 files becomes 51 across 22, and DTO-typed parameters rise from 134 to 149. accounting.controller.ts goes from 15 to 0.

V2.2.1 stays FAIL and no verdict moves: the matrix is 39 NOT_ASSESSED / 129 PASS / 88 NOT_APPLICABLE / 89 FAIL against main, with V8.2.4 the only rejected decision - main's standing drift, repaired on security/login-lockout-finding-4459.

accounting-api.dto.spec.ts passes 33 of 33; the accounting suite passes 217 with none newly skipped; tsc --noEmit on apps/api exits 0; the cryptographic inventory is regenerated and discover-cryptography.test.mjs passes 8 of 8; guard=0.
